title: Letters on a Phone Keypad

concept.title: One digit, one choice among its letters
body: On an old phone keypad every digit stands for a few letters: `2` is `abc`, `3` is `def`, `4` is `ghi`, `5` is `jkl`, `6` is `mno`, `7` is `pqrs`, `8` is `tuv`, `9` is `wxyz`. A string of digits stands for many words: for every digit you choose **one** of its letters.
That is a search with a fixed depth, one level for each digit. At level `pos`, try each letter of the digit, add it to the word, recurse on the next digit, and take it away again:
The number of words is the product of the letter counts (at most `4^6 = 4096` here). Going through the letters of a key in alphabetical order puts the words in dictionary order.

statement: A phone keypad has these letters: 2 = abc, 3 = def, 4 = ghi, 5 = jkl, 6 = mno, 7 = pqrs, 8 = tuv, 9 = wxyz. Given a string of digits from 2 to 9, print all words (one letter for every digit) that it can stand for, in dictionary order, one word per line.
inputFormat: The only line has the digits.
outputFormat: All words in dictionary order, one per line.

examples.output:
ad
ae
af
bd
be
bf
cd
ce
cf
examples.note: The words are ad ae af bd be bf cd ce cf.

hints: Handle the digits from left to right: one level of recursion per digit.
For the current digit try each of its letters in alphabetical order.
When all digits are used, the word is complete.

explanation: Level `pos` of the recursion chooses the letter for digit number `pos`. After the last digit the word is recorded. Alphabetical order of the letters gives dictionary order of the words.
solution.complexity: Time O(number of words * length), at most 4096 words.
